state.context: Required behavior for CanFeedback comprises preserved suggestion authors, undisclosed voting identities, reliable aggregate totals, idempotent vote withdrawal/casting, historical moderation evidence, limited contribution traffic, duplicates that leave votes on their original suggestion, and an urgent incident destination owned by support. The language specifies that permanent deletion cannot remove an unconditionally locked row; retained archives remain in unique constraints; admission decisions use bounded owner scans; a CRUD create hook sees normalized staged creation; scenario writes do not trigger such hooks; created comes with every record. No declared mechanism detects private details automatically. Today's source combines locked Vote.account with remove deletion in unvote, and validates duplicate links only against self/cross-product references. The actual Desk create authority is by=support with can_work(actor,row.location), so it cannot serve ordinary member intake. Its responsible worker is introducing exported desk.open_request by=authenticated, checking a verified email and live Location. A direct canonical form can use that operation with separately entered private incident content, without extracting feedback text or elevating the caller. Plan A preserves the unique suggestion/account Vote and introduces active and cast_at. Account stays locked; generated Vote writes are disabled. Casting creates or reactivates the caller's row and records now, provided all their retained/archived Votes satisfy cast_at<=now-10s; withdrawal only clears active. Aggregation includes active votes. Suggestions have one creation path: its precommit hook counts the pending submission and archived author submissions in the last hour, accepting a maximum of five. Suggestions begin hidden=true; editing pending own text is allowed when moderation_reason==null; product owners publish/hide with a persisted reason; hidden rows have no public read grant. Nonnull duplicate links must point to a distinct same-product suggestion that itself has no duplicate. Dependent invariant checking stops a referenced root being linked elsewhere, so no chains or cycles result; vote rows and authors never move. Plan B keeps deleting votes by removing their account lock, adds persistent attempt models for hourly submission/vote counters, exposes newly created suggestions publicly before staff review, and uses a bounded ancestor check that allows acyclic duplicate chains. Both plans still require concrete Can/desired-JS declarations and examples, with no compiler/stdlib implementation. Select according to the stated requirements and acknowledge unverified runtime semantics. Support has implemented the exported intake, with its literal contract and conditions recorded in the attached source fragment.
state.canonical_support_source:
export scenario open_request(location:Location,subject:Ticket.subject,body:Message.body,category:text,priority:Ticket.priority=normal,attachments:file[]=[],client:Customer?=null label="Customer"@{nl="Klant"}) -> Ticket by=authenticated label="Open support request"@{nl="Supportverzoek openen"}
   require actor.email_verified and location.active and trim(body)!="" and trim(category)!=""
   require client==null or (client.active and location in client.locations and (owns(actor,client) or has_role(actor,client,administrator) or has_role(actor,client,booker)))
   require count(Ticket archived=include as ticket where ticket.email==actor.email and ticket.created>now-1d)<20
   do
    create Ticket {location,customer=client,subject,email=actor.email,thread=operation.id,category,priority,queue="Reception"} as ticket
    create Message {parent=ticket,external_id=format("web-{id}",{id=operation.id}),kind=customer,body,sender=actor.email,recipient=null,author=actor,attachments} as message
    return ticket

feedback_design.instructions: Assess these two approaches against required journeys, disclosure protection, historical integrity, traffic safeguards and drafting cost; which should be adopted?

criteria.A: Keep vote identities while toggling activity, impose caller-wide casting spacing and a creation cap, require publication review and disallow duplicate chains through root-only references; no attempt ledger is needed, while ancestry flexibility and hourly casting counts are unavailable.
criteria.B: Unlock and remove votes, persist separate request-attempt entities, initially show suggestions and later hide abuse, and check bounded duplicate ancestry; exact hourly traffic and chains become possible with larger state and unreviewed public content.
